en: Us factory women are all poor.
Every one of us cares more about a crust of
bread than about world peace tomorrow.
I've got a kid, but
she won't warm to me one bit.
The moment she was born, my husband just
up and vanished. Ever since, all on my own,
I've been raising her, and yet...
Honestly, she hasn't got a sweet bone
in her body.
Oh, spare me your pity.
It only makes me feel more wretched.
Day after day, nothing good ever happens.
We poor folk grieve at being born
and rejoice at dying...
Many's the time I've wanted to die.
But if I died, what on earth would
become of my kid? Thinking of that,
I just can't go through with it.
She won't warm to me, but she's still my own.
Who are you?
I'll tell you now, I've got no business
with the likes of you.
Just what reason have you got
for prowling round a place like this?
What business has someone rich like you
got in a place like this?
You're an odd one, you are.
If I'd been born into money
like you, would I have been any
happier, I wonder?
Rich folk like you
have never known hard times, have you?
Who's there
A-a thief?
Hah, in a house like this? There's not one
thing here I'd miss if it got stolen...
Then I shall help myself, without a qualm.
To your blood, that is...
Wh-what...?
What on earth are you saying?!
M-murd...
Y-you...
you
murderer!!
P-please,
I beg you,
my daughter,
not Jill,
don't lay
a hand on her
You have a slanderous tongue, woman.
I do not kill.
You will merely do as I say.
For as long as you live, that is.
I'm off to work now.
What sort of work do you do?
You looking for a job too? Not likely.
But, well, if you come by where I work,
I'll show you what sort of work I do.
Come on down to the factory.
What sort of work I do there?
I'll show you.
Well, another day of getting gummed up
with gelatine is waiting for me...
Someone rich like you, wandering about
in these parts...
that's very strange...
I'm Martha. Just a poor factory hand.
You're curious what sort of work I do,
aren't you?
One of these days, I'll show you properly...
Come to the factory... and I'll show you
all sorts of things.
Me, I wish I'd been born into money
like you.
This factory muck just won't come off.
Honestly, what a miserable job.
And then we make glue out of that gelatine.
Forget world peace, a crust of bread,
